description.value: The study examined brain activity and psychological measures related to binge eating before and four months after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery in women with severe obesity, compared with BMI-matched women who did not undergo treatment.

design.value: Prospective longitudinal fMRI study with assessments approximately 1 month before and 4 months after bariatric surgery, using 15 women who opted for RYGB and 13 BMI-matched women who did not undergo treatment. Participants were classified as binge eating or non-binge eating, yielding RYGB BE, RYGB NB, NT BE, and NT NB groups.

name.value: Questionnaire of Eating and Weight Patterns Revised (QEWP-R)

description.value: Used to assess binge eating status at baseline and follow-up.
Used with the QEWP-R to classify participants according to binge eating criteria at baseline.
Used at 4 months to reassess binge eating status and included modified questions pertaining to bariatric surgery.
Participants were assessed according to the DSM-5 and classified as BE if they endorsed overeating with loss of control and met full or subthreshold criteria.

The EMAQ assesses emotional eating in response to both positive and negative emotions and situations. Mean scores are calculated for positive emotions and situations and negative emotions and situations.

The PFS assesses the impact of current food-abundant environments, including appetite-related thoughts, feelings, and motivations, at three levels of food proximity: food available, food present, and food tasted.

name.value: Tanita scale employing bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA)

description.value: Used to measure body weight and body fat at baseline and 4 months post-surgery.
Women with obesity who opted for RYGB surgery.

exclusion_criteria.value: absence of diabetes, heart disease, cancer, sleep apnea, and normal/well-controlled blood pressure

10% weight fluctuation in the previous three months; pregnancy, lactation, planning to become pregnant in next 18 months, or <1 year postpartum; smoking cessation in the previous three months or smoking more than five cigarettes per week; known claustrophobia for an fMRI enclosure; metal implants, non-removable metallic dental retainers, or pacemakers; consumption of four or more alcoholic drinks per day; recreational drug use in the previous six months; history of anorexia nervosa; history of hospitalization for a psychiatric condition; history of alcohol or drug dependence; previous bariatric surgery

task_description.value: Visual stimuli were presented in six runs. Each run was made up of 10 stimuli of the same type (HEF, LEF, NF) and repeated twice with different stimuli. Ten stimuli were presented for four seconds each, with a 52-s pre-stimulus baseline and a 40-s post-stimulus baseline.

design_type.value: pseudorandom visual stimulus presentation in six runs

stimuli.value: HEF stimuli included cakes, ice cream, and fast foods; LEF stimuli consisted of fruits and vegetables; NF stimuli consisted of basic office supplies, such as tape, staplers, and rubber bands.

instrument.value: 1.5 GE Tesla twin-speed scanner with supine quadrature RF head coil

description.value: Functional T2*-weighted images with a gradient echo pulse sequence were obtained. During each run, 36 whole-brain scans were taken, each consisting of 25 contiguous slices, 4 mm thick, parallel to the AC/PC line.

Prior to statistical analyses, the realigned T2*-weighted volumes were slice-time corrected, spatially transformed to a standardized brain (Montreal Neurologic Institute), and smoothed with an 8-mm full-width half-maximum Gaussian kernel.

steps.value: spatial transformation to a standardized Montreal Neurologic Institute brain
smoothing with an 8-mm full-width half-maximum Gaussian kernel

model_settings.value: First-level regressors were created by convolving the onset of each condition with the canonical HRF with duration of 40 s. Contrasts were created for Food > NF and HEF > LEF at baseline, 4 months post, and Timepoint 1 > Timepoint 2.

model_type.value: group random effects model; 2nd-level multiple regression analyses

model_settings.value: Predictor variables were experimental group (BE vs. NB; RYGB vs. NT) and BMI as a nuisance covariate. Main comparisons included overall effects of experimental group at baseline, 4 months post-surgery, and baseline > post contrasts, as well as two-way interactions between experimental and intervention groups.

estimator.value: nonparametric bootstrapping; one thousand bootstrap samples with a bias corrected and accelerated confidence interval

model_settings.value: Nine ROIs consisted of 10 mm radius spheres centered at MNI coordinates. Mean BOLD signal was extracted for each ROI.
